title: Apple's Diwali AirPods 5 Brings a Rangoli-Engraved Case to India at Rs 17,900
excerpt: The India-exclusive special edition costs the same as the standard model, is capped at two pairs per customer, and anchors a festive campaign that includes free rangoli workshops in the US, Canada, Malaysia and Singapore.
body:
• Apple has launched a special-edition AirPods 5 with Wireless Charging Case for Diwali in India, with a rangoli-inspired engraving around a heart-eyes emoji on the case.
  • It costs Rs 17,900 — the same as the standard AirPods 5 with Wireless Charging Case — and is on sale from October 11 to November 11, 2026, while stocks last, limited to two pairs per customer.
  • It is an India exclusive, sold only through Apple's online store, the Apple Store app and six stores: BKC and Borivali in Mumbai, Saket and Noida in Delhi NCR, Hebbal in Bengaluru and Koregaon Park in Pune.
  • Diaspora tie-in: Apple is running free rangoli workshops — designed with artist Arushi Kathuria, using Procreate on iPad — from October 14 to November 9 in India and at selected stores in the US, Canada, Malaysia and Singapore.

Apple has opened its Diwali season in India with a product made only for this market: a special-edition AirPods 5 with Wireless Charging Case, its case engraved with a rangoli-inspired design arranged around a heart-eyes emoji. The edition went on sale October 11 and runs to November 11, 2026, subject to stock, according to MacRumors. The price is Rs 17,900 — identical to the standard AirPods 5 with Wireless Charging Case, so the engraving carries no premium.

What you get — and the fine print

The hardware is the standard fifth-generation model Apple introduced in September: open-ear Active Noise Cancellation that Apple says removes up to 50% more noise than AirPods 4 with ANC, next-generation Adaptive EQ, Live Translation and hands-free Siri AI, per Apple's launch release. The wireless charging case supports USB-C, Qi and Apple Watch chargers and provides up to 22 hours of listening time with ANC on. The special edition's terms matter: purchases are capped at two pairs per customer; it is excluded from other AirPods promotions and from Business, Education and Corporate Employee Purchase Plan pricing; and Apple cautions that a repair or replacement may be fulfilled with a standard-edition unit, depending on supply — the engraving is not guaranteed to survive a service visit.

How to buy it

There is exactly one channel set: Apple's online store and the Apple Store app in India, plus the six Apple retail stores — BKC and Borivali in Mumbai, Saket and Noida in Delhi NCR, Hebbal in Bengaluru and Koregaon Park in Pune. It is not sold through authorised resellers, and it does not appear as a normal variant on the AirPods buy page; Apple lists it under its store's festive offerings. The launch sits inside a wider festive campaign running October 11 to November 11, with instant cashback of up to Rs 15,000 on select products with eligible cards and no-cost EMI options across iPhone, Mac, iPad, Watch and AirPods lines.

The diaspora angle: rangoli workshops abroad

The part of this launch aimed outside India is the workshops. Apple has created free Today at Apple rangoli sessions with artist Arushi Kathuria, in which participants draw rangoli designs in Procreate on iPad with Apple Pencil, using a custom brush that mimics coloured powder. Sessions run October 14 to November 9 in India and at selected locations in the United States, Canada, Malaysia and Singapore — a Diwali programme diaspora families can actually attend, even though the engraved AirPods themselves cannot be bought outside India.

What's next

Stock is the variable: the edition is limited, capped per customer, and Apple has already signalled replacements may default to the standard model. If you want the rangoli case as a Diwali gift, the practical advice from Apple's own terms is simple — buy early in the window, and keep the standard edition in mind as the fallback at the same price.
